parameters.name: Enable
parameters.description: Enables or disables the DHCP Client entry.

parameters.name: Interface
parameters.description: {{reference}} The IP Interface associated with the ''Client'' entry.

parameters.name: Status
parameters.description: The status of this table entry. {{enum}} The {{enum|Error_Misconfigured}} value indicates that a necessary configuration value is undefined or invalid. The {{enum|Error}} value MAY be used by the CPE to indicate a locally defined error condition.

parameters.name: DHCPStatus
parameters.description: The DHCP Client status as defined in {{bibref|RFC2131}}. {{enum}} Note: This value is only relevant when the DHCP Client is operationally enabled (i.e. when {{param|Status}} is {{enum|Enabled|Status}}).

parameters.name: IPAddress
parameters.description: IPv4 Address option received from the DHCP Server. {{empty}} when {{param|Status}} is not equal to {{enum|Bound|DHCPStatus}}.

parameters.name: SubnetMask
parameters.description: Subnet mask option received from the DHCP Server. {{empty}} when {{param|Status}} is not equal to {{enum|Bound|DHCPStatus}}. Value is information received via DHCP Option 1.

parameters.name: IPRouters
parameters.description: {{list}} Items represent IP Router IPv4 Address(es) received from the DHCP server. {{empty}} when {{param|Status}} is not equal to {{enum|Bound|DHCPStatus}}. Value is information received via DHCP Options 3, 33 or 121.

parameters.name: DNSServers
parameters.description: {{list}} Items represent DNS Server IPv4 Address(es) received from the DHCP server. {{empty}} when {{param|Status}} is not equal to {{enum|Bound|DHCPStatus}}. Value is information received via DHCP Option 6.

parameters.name: LeaseTimeRemaining
parameters.description: DHCP lease time remaining in {{units}}. A value of -1 indicates an infinite lease.

parameters.name: DHCPServer
parameters.description: The IPv4 address of the current DHCP server.

parameters.name: PassthroughEnable
parameters.description: If {{false}}, the DHCP Client retrieved IP address information is configured on the referenced {{param|Interface}} object. If {{true}}, the DHCP Client retrieved information is propagated to the parameters in the referenced {{param|PassthroughDHCPPool}} object, replacing any existing configuration (including ''MinAddress'', ''MaxAddress'', ''SubnetMask'', ''IPRouters'', and ''DNSServers'').

parameters.name: PassthroughDHCPPool
parameters.description: {{reference}}When {{param}} is set to {{empty}}, {{param|PassthroughEnable}} MUST be set to {{false}} (i.e. passthrough can not be enabled without a pool reference specified).

parameters.name: AuthenticationProtocol
parameters.description: Specifies the authentication mechanism to be used.

parameters.name: DSCPMark
parameters.description: Diffserv code point to be used for outgoing DHCP messages.

object.description: This object contains DHCP client settings for an associated ''IP Interface'' indicated by {{param|Interface}}. For enabled table entries, if {{param|Interface}} is not a valid reference then the table entry is inoperable and the CPE MUST set {{param|Status}} to {{enum|Error_Misconfigured|Status}}. Note: The {{object}} table includes a unique key parameter that is a strong reference. If a strongly referenced object is deleted, the CPE will set the referencing parameter to {{empty}}. However, doing so under these circumstances might cause the updated {{object}} row to then violate the table's unique key constraint; if this occurs, the CPE MUST set {{param|Status}} to {{enum|Error_Misconfigured|Status}} and disable the offending {{object}} row.
